claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: Let q=min(m,n). In the unit-cost arithmetic model, a two-dimensional prefix table costs O(mn) and gives every square sum in O(1). For candidate L>0, scanning all (m-L+1)(n-L+1)<=mn placements proves feasibility. For each integer l with L<l<=q, validating one in-range placement with sum greater than k proves that l is infeasible; these q-L checks cost O(q)<=O(mn). Acceptance therefore proves that L is feasible and every larger side is infeasible. Conversely, a true optimum supplies such a witness at every larger side. For the sentinel L=0, feasibility is deliberately omitted and witnesses for every positive side prove that no positive side is feasible. No sign or monotonicity assumption is used. The claim is a word-operation statement, not an unbounded-bit-time statement.
claims.witness: Candidate L together with one violating square coordinate for every side l>L; for L=0, one for every positive side.
claims.search_method: Independent quantifier proof plus exhaustive exact-integer testing on signed matrices and thresholds.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: After prefix preprocessing, independently scanning sides q,q-1,...,1 and returning the first side without a violation returns the maximum feasible side even when feasibility is nonmonotone. Assuming m>=n=q and writing d=q-L, a complete scan at side n-t has exactly (m-n+t+1)(t+1) placements. Thus the work is bounded by sum_{t=0}^d (m-n+t+1)(t+1)=O((m-n+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3), plus O(mn) preprocessing. Since d<=q and q<=m, this is O(mnq), and it is O(mn) for d=O(1). When L=0, the displayed sum includes one unused side-zero term (m+1)(n+1), so it remains a valid upper bound. Retaining the first violation at each rejected side constructs claim 0's certificate.
claims.witness: The descending scan returns L and retains one encountered violating placement for each tested larger side.
claims.search_method: Algebraic placement-count derivation and exhaustive comparison against brute-force optima.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: In the n-by-n alternating-row family, a square avoiding the first row has sum zero. A square meeting it has the sum of a length-l alternating interval: zero for even l and either 1 or -1 for odd l. At least one odd-l placement has value 1, so F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l. With k=0, feasibility therefore alternates at every consecutive side. For the greedy counterexample with k=1, the two side-2 sums are 1 and 4. A left-to-right scan passes the first, decreases to side 1 at the second, and subsequently encounters only entries at most 1; it returns 1 without revisiting the initial entry 2. Yet side 2 is infeasible because of sum 4 and side 1 is infeasible because 2>1, so the sentinel optimum is 0.
claims.witness: k=1 and matrix [[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]]; its side-2 sums are [1,4], while the already-passed top-left entry is the side-1 violation 2.
claims.search_method: Exact alternating-interval proof, exact checks for n=1 through 40, and literal simulation of the no-revisit trace.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, an l-square sum is X·Y, where X and Y are independently chosen length-l window sums of u and v. The maximum of xy over two finite one-dimensional sets occurs among the four products of their minima and maxima. All extrema for one l cost O(m+n), hence all q lengths cost O(q(m+n))<=2mn. A nonzero pivot p=A_rc recognizes the class through pA_ij=A_icA_rj. Using the pivot column and row, each square sum is a corresponding numerator divided exactly by p; taking the maximum after dividing all four corner numerators handles p<0 correctly. The all-zero case is immediate. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, an l-square sum is l(X+Y), so F_l=l(max X+max Y), with the same time bound. The identity A_ij=A_i1+A_1j-A_11 recognizes additive separability in O(mn). Thus recognition plus optimization is O(mn) word operations for both classes.
claims.witness: The product identity sum_{i,j}u_i v_j=(sum_i u_i)(sum_j v_j) and additive identity sum_{i,j}(u_i+v_j)=l(sum_i u_i+sum_j v_j).
claims.search_method: Symbolic factorization and recognition proofs plus exhaustive signed factorization, negative-pivot, zero, and arbitrary-matrix checks.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For l=B-t and horizontal start s, telescoping the supported row gives p_{s+l}-p_s=p_{B-j}-p_i with i=s, j=t-s. If i,j<N, the value is C+x_i+y_j>=C-2W=1. If i>=N, then p_i=H while p_{B-j}=C+y_j<=C+W=H-1, making the value negative. If j>=N, then p_{B-j}=-H and p_i=-x_i, giving x_i-H<0. Both indices cannot be invalid because i+j=t<=2N-2. The three arbitrary middle prefixes are never endpoints: i<=2N-2 and B-j>=2N+2. Squares avoiding the supported row sum to zero, which cannot exceed the positive valid windows. Consequently F_{B-t}=C+max_{i+j=t}(x_i+y_j). Under threshold C+K, the maximum feasible mapped side is B minus the least t with c_t<=K; if none exists, every mapped side is infeasible. The embedding is exact, though its B-by-B dense representation does not itself yield a fine-grained lower bound.
claims.witness: The B=4N prefix-difference construction from the draft; the unused middle prefixes were also tested with (0,0,0), (999,-777,345), and (-1000000,1000000,-314159).
claims.search_method: Complete endpoint-range case split plus exhaustive exact-integer coefficient and threshold checks for vectors over {-2,-1,0,2} through length 3.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: In the explicit-binary bit-cost model, consider the 1-by-1 equality input a=k=2^(B-1). Its positive optimum is 1. If a deterministic exact algorithm's equality execution leaves any lower bit r unread, replacing a by k+2^r preserves every inspected bit but changes the correct result to the no-positive-side sentinel 0. The algorithm would behave identically on inputs requiring different answers, a contradiction. Hence all B-1 lower positions must be inspected on this input, giving Omega(B) bit cost even when mn=1. This excludes a bit-time O(mn) bound independent of integer length, but correctly does not exclude O(mn) word operations.
claims.witness: For every 0<=r<B-1, the pair a=k=2^(B-1) and a'=2^(B-1)+2^r differs in one lower bit and has the opposite 1-by-1 answer.
claims.search_method: Decision-tree indistinguishability proof with exact one-bit checks for B=2 through 128.

target_evidence: The exact target requests either a general O(mn)-time algorithm for signed integer matrices or a matching impossibility result under a stated standard assumption. The draft supplies neither for the substantive bounded-word/unit-cost problem: its general search is O(mn min(m,n)); its O(mn) algorithms cover only two special separable classes; and its one-row embedding expands length-N vectors to a dense Theta(N^2)-cell matrix and establishes no incompatible conditional lower bound. Claim 5 is a correct generic input-representation lower bound only when bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged; it expressly leaves O(mn) word operations possible and is therefore too model-dependent and coarse to resolve the intended endpoint. These are material, correct advances, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS rather than NO_VALID_PROGRESS is warranted. The final writeup explicitly states that the main endpoint remains unresolved and labels the result partial, so claimed_resolution PARTIAL is ACCURATE and is not overclaimed.
